images.title: Distinguished Service Order — NAM 1967-02-22--1
images.evidence: The museum describes a silver-gilt alisee cross with white enamel, gold edging, a red central cypher roundel and green-and-gold wreath, with suspension and ribbon. The object-page heading gives 1900, while its body refers to an announcement dated 1901-09-27 and says the recipient died on 1901-02-25. These dates conflict; no individual award date is asserted.

images.title: Victory Medal 1914–19 — NAM 1998-05-27-4
images.evidence: The National Army Museum identifies this medal in Major Oliver Stewart’s Royal Flying Corps group. It describes Winged Victory on the obverse, ‘The Great War for Civilisation’ on the reverse and a rainbow ribbon; it notes that the medal was issued with the British War Medal rather than singly. 1914–19 denotes the medal’s commemorated war period, not an individual award date.

images.title: Meritorious Service Medal — NAM 1989-03-77-2
images.evidence: The medal is identified with Sergeant Major John Wing of the 17th Foot and dated 1847. The National Army Museum states that the medal was instituted in 1845 and that the ribbon was crimson until 1916, when white edging and a central stripe were introduced. 1847 is the dated museum object; 1845 is the institution date stated by the museum.

images.title: Royal Red Cross — Auckland Museum 2001.25.863-3
images.evidence: Auckland Museum identifies the object as a first-class Royal Red Cross awarded to Matron Cora B. Anderson, NZANS, and dates the award to 1919. The complete cross and lady’s bow ribbon are shown. The museum’s circa 1918/1919 object record and award identification are retained as given.
